papers.title: Codeveloping a Clinical Pathway for Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection With Primary Care Providers: User-Centered Design Study.
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the most common cause of health care-associated infectious diarrhea; however, variability in laboratory testing results in uncertainty in diagnosis and clinical decision-making. Recurrent CDI (rCDI), defined as the return of infection following initial treatment, continues to present significant clinical challenges due to limited therapeutic options. Although health care providers are familiar with vancomycin as first-line therapy for CDI, many are less familiar with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), despite its recommendation in clinical guide
papers.summary: This user-centered design study engaged primary care providers to co-develop a clinical pathway for managing recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI). The work addresses diagnostic uncertainty from variable laboratory testing and limited provider familiarity with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), despite its guideline recommendation. The resulting pathway aims to standardize and improve rCDI care in primary care settings.

papers.title: Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort.
papers.abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. However, rarefaction has been strongly criticized, leading to the development of compositional data analysis and normalization methods. Therefore, I reassessed the benchmarking data that were generated by the developers of one such method, robust Aitchison PCA. I found num
papers.summary: This study reanalyzes benchmarking data originally used to promote robust Aitchison PCA and finds that simple rarefaction actually controls for uneven sequencing depth better than compositional data analysis methods. The author argues that rarefaction, despite past criticism, remains the most effective approach for handling variable sequencing effort in amplicon studies.

papers.title: Strollur: an R package for working with amplicon sequence data in R.
papers.abstract: Microbiologists are increasingly relying on R to analyze and visualize amplicon sequence data from microbiome studies. We present strollur, which is an open-source package that facilitates the import, export, and handling of amplicon sequence data within the R programming language.
papers.summary: Strollur is a new open-source R package designed to streamline the import, export, and manipulation of amplicon sequence data from microbiome studies. It aims to make it easier for microbiologists to work with such data directly within the R environment.

papers.title: Activity and diversity of sulfate- and methane-based pathways of anaerobic chitin and N-acetylglucosamine degradation in marine sediments.
papers.abstract: Sulfate reduction is estimated to account for half of the organic carbon respiration in anoxic, organic-rich ocean sediments. Sulfate-reducing microorganisms (SRMs) typically oxidize simple carbon compounds, such as primary alcohols, or small fatty acids. However, much of the organic input to the seafloor is complex, driving interactions between terminal respirers, such as SRMs and methanogens, and primary degraders that initiate the breakdown of complex organic carbon. To explore how these interactions shape sediment microbiomes, we conducted multi-month microcosm experiments using serially d
papers.summary: This study used long-term microcosm experiments with marine sediments to track how sulfate-reducing and methane-producing microbial communities degrade complex carbon sources like chitin and N-acetylglucosamine. The authors found that these anaerobic degradation pathways involve diverse interacting microbial groups, with sulfate reducers and methanogens relying on primary degraders to break down complex organic matter. The work highlights how microbial interactions, rather than single-organism metabolism, shape carbon cycling in anoxic seafloor sediments.

papers.title: Integrative holo-omic data analysis predicts interactions across the host-microbiome axis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the interplay between host organisms and their microbiomes is central to the development of sustainable food systems. However, high dimensionality and spurious associations remain major obstacles to extracting meaningful biological insight from multi-omic host-associated microbiome data; a challenge further exacerbated when "holo-omic" analyses across the host-microbiome boundary are considered. Here, we show that a computational method designed for multi-omic analysis in eukaryotes can be leveraged to integrate and analyze five layers of holo-omic data from porcine hosts and the
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that a computational method originally designed for multi-omic analysis in eukaryotes can be adapted to integrate five layers of holo-omic data spanning both a porcine host and its microbiome. The approach aims to overcome challenges of high dimensionality and spurious associations in host-microbiome multi-omic data, enabling prediction of interactions across the host-microbiome axis. The work has implications for sustainable food systems by improving how we extract biological insight from complex holo-omic datasets.

papers.title: Functional-Taxonomic Scaling Resolves Conflicting Average Genome Size Estimates Across Environmental Gradients.
papers.abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. Here, we introduce and validate a framework that adjudicates conflicting AGS estimates by testing which estimate yields a gap between scaled functional diversity and scaled taxonomic diversity that is consistent with the expected positive association between genome size and gene functional breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates align with this framework and e
papers.summary: The authors introduce a framework to resolve conflicting estimates of community-level average genome size (AGS) from metagenomic data by testing which estimate produces a functional-taxonomic diversity gap consistent with the expected positive link between genome size and gene functional breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates align with this framework, helping adjudicate between divergent methods.

papers.title: Microbial filtering and functional reprogramming in soil exposed to spent NCM battery black powder.
papers.abstract: Spent lithium-ion battery black powder is an emerging complex contaminant, which contains transition metals, residual electrolyte salts, and compounds derived from organic electrolytes or binders. Its ecological effects on soil microbiomes remain poorly understood. Here, we designed a soil microcosm experiment with using red soil exposed to a concentration gradient of black powder derived from nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) lithium-ion batteries. Samples were collected at two incubation time points and analyzed by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Black powder exposure produced a nonlinear taxono
papers.summary: This study used soil microcosms and shotgun metagenomic sequencing to examine how spent NCM lithium-ion battery black powder affects soil microbial communities. Exposure caused nonlinear taxonomic shifts, with microbial filtering and functional reprogramming of the soil microbiome. The findings highlight ecological risks of this emerging complex contaminant.

papers.title: Clinical severity score-guided metagenomic analysis identifying gut microbial taxonomic and functional markers for severe hepatitis E progression.
papers.abstract: Although gut microbiome alterations have been reported in hepatitis E (HE), the taxonomic and functional determinants of disease severity remain poorly defined. Here, we performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 125 individuals spanning acute non-icteric hepatitis (ANIH), acute icteric hepatitis (AIH), acute liver failure (ALF), and healthy controls. We constructed a surrogate clinical severity index from routine blood parameters and developed an integrative analytical framework that combined XGBoost-based taxonomic modeling with LASSO-driven functional feature selection t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 125 individuals to identify gut microbial taxonomic and functional markers associated with hepatitis E severity. By combining a clinical severity index with XGBoost and LASSO modeling, the authors linked specific microbial features to progression from mild to severe liver disease. The work highlights the potential of microbiome-based markers for stratifying hepatitis E patients.

papers.title: Design and evaluation of a streamlined enrichment method for faster co-detection of enteric bacterial pathogens in natural soils and environmental samples.
papers.abstract: This study developed a streamlined, sensitive and rapid method for co-detection of low concentrations of Salmonella enterica, Shigella flexneri, Listeria monocytogenes, and pathogenic Escherichia coli from soil. First, autoclaved soil from Iowa with serial dilutions of bacteria to confirm individual species recovery rates on selective agar by qPCR under varying primary enrichment times was used. All pathogens were detected by qPCR of colonies recovered from replicate sterile soils spiked with 10^1 or greater bacteria within 5 hours of enrichment. Shiga toxin expressing E. coli (STEC) and L. mo
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study presents a streamlined enrichment workflow that enables simultaneous detection of four enteric bacterial pathogens (Salmonella, Shigella, Listeria, and pathogenic E. coli) from soil samples within about 5 hours. Using selective agar combined with qPCR after primary enrichment, the method reliably detected pathogens at concentrations as low as 10 CFU per sample, offering a faster alternative to conventional culture-based approaches.

papers.title: Microbes on the Mind: Multi-modal Neuroimaging Reveals Gut-Brain Axes in Infants.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome undergoes rapid maturation after birth and has been associated with cognition and mental health, yet its relation to early brain development remains poorly defined. We analyzed 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years with multimodal MRI and paired fecal shotgun metagenomics. Microbiome-wide association analyses identified associations with cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity. Ridge-regularized canonical correlation analysis identified two principal covariance patterns: a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic m
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study paired fecal metagenomics with multimodal MRI in 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years to test whether gut microbiome composition relates to early brain development. Microbiome-wide association analyses linked microbial features to cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity, and canonical correlation analysis revealed two main gut-brain covariance patterns (a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic mode). The work provides some of the earliest evidence for gut-brain axis coupling during infancy.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for protein database indexes that reduces the memory footprint of the Ferragina-Manzini index by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable speed for metagenomic taxonomic classification. The new run-block compression scheme scales better with alphabet size, making it practical to index large RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein datasets.

papers.title: Long-Read Metagenomic Characterization of the Microbial DNA and Resistome Recovered from a Peracetic Acid Immersion Chiller in a Commercial Poultry Processing Facility: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Peracetic acid (PAA)-based immersion chillers are a critical pathogen intervention in commercial poultry processing, yet the microbial DNA recoverable from these systems remains poorly characterized. Here, we applied long-read Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) metagenomics to characterize the taxonomic composition, resistance gene content, and mobile element context of the microbial DNA recovered from the mid-stage immersion chiller of a commercial poultry processing facility. From 14.47 GB of sequencing data (median Q-score 19.1), we reconstructed three near-complete metagenome-assembled genom
papers.summary: This pilot study used long-read Oxford Nanopore metagenomics to characterize the microbial DNA and resistance genes (resistome) present in a peracetic acid immersion chiller at a commercial poultry processing facility. From 14.47 GB of sequencing data, the authors reconstructed three near-complete metagenome-assembled genomes, providing a first look at the taxonomic composition and mobile genetic element context of antimicrobial resistance genes in this critical pathogen intervention system.

papers.title: MOSHPIT: Accessible, reproducible metagenome data science on the QIIME 2 framework.
papers.abstract: Metagenome sequencing has revolutionized functional microbiome analysis across diverse ecosystems but is fraught with technical hurdles. We introduce MOSHPIT (MOdular SHotgun metagenome Pipelines with Integrated provenance Tracking; https://moshpit.qiime2.org)-software built on the QIIME 2/rachis framework (Q2F) that integrates best-in-class CAMI II- and LEMMI-validated metagenome tools with robust provenance tracking and multiple user interfaces-enabling streamlined, reproducible metagenome analysis for all expertise levels. By building on Q2F, MOSHPIT enhances scalability, interoperability,
papers.summary: MOSHPIT is a new software package built on the QIIME 2 framework that integrates validated shotgun metagenome analysis tools with built-in provenance tracking and multiple user interfaces. It aims to make reproducible, scalable metagenome data science accessible to researchers at all expertise levels.

papers.title: Coincidental observation of a parvovirus during a targeted bacterial survey of cattle suffering from septic arthritis.
papers.abstract: DNA capture-based sequencing by hybridization probe enrichment (CapSeq) affords high-throughput and targeted gene-to-organism detection. Despite the specificity designed into CapSeq platforms, untargeted DNA represent additional genes and organisms of interest. To this end, de novo metagenome assemblies of CapSeq datasets present opportunities for discovery. We report an example here. CapSeq of samples that originated from cattle suffering from septic arthritis resulted in detection and assembly of two ungulate tetraparvovirus 1 (UTPV1) genomes. These coincidental detections and assemblies wer
papers.summary: During a targeted bacterial survey of cattle with septic arthritis, researchers unexpectedly assembled two complete genomes of ungulate tetraparvovirus 1 (UTPV1) from off-target reads in their capture-based sequencing data. This demonstrates that hybridization-capture datasets contain useful untargeted metagenomic information that can be mined for viral discovery.

papers.title: Improving Metagenomics Classification with Kmask: Entropy-Based Masking of Low-Complexity Regions.
papers.abstract: Accurate taxonomic classification in metagenomics is often compromised by low-complexity sequences, which lead to chance matches that in turn cause sequences to be misclassified. Here we present Kmask, an entropy-based masking tool implemented for use either standalone or as part of Kraken [1,2] database construction, which replaces low-entropy regions with Ns. Using a sliding window size aligned with Kraken's default k-mer length and parameters optimized across 12 control bacterial genomes spanning a broad range of GC content, Kmask efficiently removes low-complexity sequences while retaining
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kmask is an entropy-based masking tool that replaces low-complexity regions in metagenomic sequences with Ns to reduce chance matches that cause misclassification. It can be used standalone or integrated into Kraken database construction, with parameters optimized across 12 control bacterial genomes spanning a broad GC range. The tool efficiently removes low-complexity sequences while retaining informative regions, improving taxonomic classification accuracy.

papers.title: "Quadrupling" the protein family space with global metagenomics.
papers.abstract: The known universe of protein families represents only a small fraction of nature's molecular diversity. From 40.3 billion predicted open reading frames across 40 446 metagenomes, 9540 metatranscriptomes, and 539 million proteins from 167 415 reference genomes, we identified 608 258 previously uncharacterized putative protein families with ≥100 members and 6.5 million families with ≥25 members, none matching known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This effort doubles the known repertoire of large families and quadruples that of smaller families. Integration of AlphaFold2-based structural pre
papers.summary: By mining over 40 billion predicted open reading frames from tens of thousands of metagenomes, metatranscriptomes, and reference genomes, the authors identified 608,258 previously uncharacterized protein families with at least 100 members, plus 6.5 million smaller families, none of which matched known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This roughly doubles the known repertoire of large protein families and quadruples that of smaller families, substantially expanding the known protein family space. The work integrates AlphaFold2-based structural predictions to help characterize these novel families.

papers.title: Native Polyethylene Biodegradation by Gut-Associated Bacteria from Galleria mellonella Larvae: Multi-Method Evidence Without Abiotic Pretreatment.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene (PE) in the environment represents a persistent ecological challenge, and the search for biological agents capable of degrading it without relying on prior abiotic pretreatment remains an active area of research. In this study, three bacterial strains-Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter hormaechei, and Acinetobacter pittii-were isolated from the gut of Galleria mellonella larvae dietarily induced with native low-density polyethylene (LDPE), without prior UV, thermal, or chemical treatment. Molecular identification was confirmed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and
papers.summary: Researchers isolated three bacterial strains (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter hormaechei, and Acinetobacter pittii) from the gut of Galleria mellonella larvae fed native low-density polyethylene, and used multiple methods to show these bacteria can degrade PE without any prior UV, thermal, or chemical pretreatment. This provides evidence that gut-associated bacteria can attack untreated plastic, which is a more realistic scenario for environmental bioremediation.

papers.title: Probe-Based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy During Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: A Translational Framework Linking Intestinal Barrier Function, Microbiota, and Clinical Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of several malignancies, but their efficacy and gastrointestinal (GI) immune-related adverse events (irAEs) vary considerably among patients. Growing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota and intestinal barrier integrity are associated with both therapeutic response and toxicity, although their causal contribution and clinical utility remain incompletely defined. Dysbiosis may disrupt epithelial homeostasis, increase intestinal permeability, and promote mucosal immune activation, potentially influencing antitumor immunity a
papers.summary: This paper proposes a translational framework using probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy (pCLE) to assess intestinal barrier function in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, linking gut barrier integrity and microbiota composition to treatment response and gastrointestinal immune-related adverse events. It argues that real-time mucosal imaging could help stratify patients and predict outcomes, though the causal relationships remain to be established.

papers.title: Effects of Heat-Killed Bifidobacterium breve B-3, a Postbiotic, on Muscle Mass-Related Parameters in Patients with Sarcopenia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Pilot Trial.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sarcopenia contributes to frailty and functional decline in older adults; however, effective adjunctive strategies remain limited. Heat-killed Bifidobacterium breve B-3 (B-3HK), a postbiotic, has shown muscle-related effects in preclinical studies; however, clinical evidence in patients with established sarcopenia is scarce. This pilot trial aimed to evaluate these clinical effects. Methods: In this 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adults aged 50-89 years with Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019-defined sarcopenia received B-3HK (2 ×
papers.summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial tested whether 24 weeks of heat-killed Bifidobacterium breve B-3 (a postbiotic) improves muscle mass-related parameters in adults aged 50-89 with sarcopenia. The study was double-blind and placebo-controlled, aiming to provide clinical evidence for a postbiotic intervention in an established sarcopenia population where effective adjunctive strategies are limited.

papers.title: Viral Metagenomic Sequencing Reveals Viral Codetection Patterns in Children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections, yet the frequency and composition of viral codetections in affected children have not been extensively profiled using unbiased sequencing approaches. Here, we performed viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs collected from 42 pediatric patients with confirmed RSV infection to characterize the codetection landscape. RSV was detected and genotyped in all specimens. Beyond RSV, we identified nine additional human respiratory viruses coexisting across the cohort; several of these fall outside th
papers.summary: This study used unbiased viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs from 42 children with confirmed RSV infection to profile which other viruses co-occur. RSV was detected and genotyped in all samples, and nine additional human respiratory viruses were found across the cohort, including some not typically covered by standard diagnostic panels. The work highlights the value of metagenomic approaches for capturing the full viral codetection landscape in pediatric respiratory infections.

papers.title: Multidimensional Physiological and Gut Microbiome Profiling Identifies Subtle Physiological Patterns in an Apparently Healthy Aging Indian Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Aging is characterized by gradual shifts in cellular and physiological processes, even in individuals who remain apparently clinically healthy. These changes reflect a coordinated decline in metabolic efficiency, immune regulation, organ function, psychological resilience, and sleep integrity, domains increasingly recognized as interconnected determinants of apparently healthy aging. This study explored age- and sex-associated patterns in multidimensional physiological domains and gut microbiota features among 45 apparently healthy middle-aged and elderly participants across four age-sex group
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled 45 apparently healthy middle-aged and elderly Indian adults across multiple physiological domains (metabolism, immunity, organ function, psychological resilience, sleep) alongside gut microbiome composition. It identified subtle age- and sex-associated patterns linking physiological decline with microbial features, even in clinically healthy individuals. The work highlights the value of multidimensional profiling for detecting early aging signatures.

papers.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Revolutionizing Probiotic Research.
papers.abstract: The microbiome, as a vast and dynamic community of microbes, is now recognized as a key regulator of host physiology, profoundly influencing health and susceptibility to disease. Accordingly, probiotics are a mainstay of prevention and treatment. But the individual complexity and dynamic specificity of an individual's microbiome make the previous "one-size-fits-all" research model completely invalid. This review systematically analyzes the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) as transformative computational tools necessary to surmount these challenges. In this
papers.summary: This review examines how AI and machine learning are being applied to probiotic research, arguing that traditional one-size-fits-all approaches fail given the complexity and individuality of the microbiome. It surveys computational tools that could enable personalized probiotic design and prediction of host responses.

papers.title: Validating a high-throughput in vitro model for culturing antibiotic-altered microbiome communities.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome plays a central role in host health, and its disruption is associated with metabolic, infectious, and immune conditions. Stool sampling is frequently used to characterize snapshots of the gut microbiota. To screen microbiota communities in vitro, multi-stage bioreactors have been developed that model distinct physiological environments along the gastrointestinal tract. However, such bioreactors are often operationally complex and provide limited throughput. Stool-derived in vitro communities offer several advantages to study microbiota due to their ease of use, high-throughp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint validates a high-throughput in vitro system for culturing stool-derived gut microbiome communities, aiming to overcome the complexity and low throughput of multi-stage bioreactors. The approach is designed to enable screening of antibiotic-perturbed microbiota communities in a simpler, scalable format. It provides a methodological foundation for studying how antibiotics alter gut microbial communities outside the host.

papers.title: Differential Signature of Gut Microbiota in Female Patients with Condyloma Acuminatum and Its Association with Persistent Human Papillomavirus Infection.
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence is a critical driver of malignant transformation, yet the potential association between gut microbiota composition and HPV clearance remains insufficiently explored. Methods: This study investigated the association between gut microbial features and HPV infection outcomes in patients with condyloma acuminatum (CA). Baseline fecal samples from 44 CA patients and 20 healthy controls underwent 16S rRNA gene sequencing, followed by a two-year clinical follow-up to stratify patients into HPV turn-negative (HPV_TN) and persistent-positive (HPV_PP) g
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA sequencing to compare gut microbiota composition between 44 women with condyloma acuminatum and 20 healthy controls, then followed patients for two years to see who cleared HPV. They found distinct microbial signatures in CA patients and associations between specific gut bacteria and whether HPV infection persisted or resolved. The work suggests gut microbiota may influence HPV clearance, though the small sample size limits conclusions.

papers.title: Longitudinal Stability of the Gut Microbiota in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a key role in immune regulation in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet longitudinal data on microbiome dynamics and their relationships with disability and biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to identify longitudinal gut microbiome changes in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) and their association with disability and specific serum biomarkers, including predicted metabolic pathways. In this prospective longitudinal study, 29 treatment-naïve RRMS patients were evaluated at baseline and after one year of disease-modifying therapy. Clinical asse
papers.summary: This prospective study tracked gut microbiome composition in 29 treatment-naive relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis patients over one year of disease-modifying therapy, examining links to disability and serum biomarkers. The findings suggest the gut microbiota remains relatively stable longitudinally, with limited associations to clinical or biomarker changes.

papers.title: Phragmites Communis (Lu Gen) Alleviates Hyperuricemia via Xanthine Oxidase Inhibition and Gut-Microbiota-Mediated Metabolite Urate Transporter Regulation.
papers.abstract: Background: Hyperuricemia (HU) results from excessive uric acid (UA) production/impaired excretion and is associated with gout and renal dysfunction. Gut microbiota dysbiosis may impair intestinal UA excretion, disrupt the gut barrier, and promote inflammation. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with multitarget and microbiota-modulating effects, may offer a therapeutic strategy for HU. In this study, the rhizome of Phragmites communis, a TCM used for clearing heat and promoting diuresis, was investigated. Specifically, we evaluated whether P. communis could alleviate HU by suppressing xanthi
papers.summary: This study shows that the traditional Chinese medicine Phragmites communis (Lu Gen) reduces hyperuricemia in a rodent model through two mechanisms: inhibiting xanthine oxidase to lower uric acid production and reshaping gut microbiota to regulate urate transporters and improve intestinal uric acid excretion. The findings support a multi-target, microbiota-mediated therapeutic strategy for hyperuricemia and gout.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Patterns: Harnessing Correspondence Analysis to Explore Maternal Lifestyle Profiles and Gestational Weight Gain.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate gestational weight gain (GWG), encompassing both low and excessive, is a significant concern because of its association with adverse maternal and neonatal health outcomes. The relationships between maternal lifestyle factors, such as diet, physical activity, prepregnancy body mass index (BMI), and GWG, are complex. This study aims to explore these associations via correspondence analysis (CA), a method that visualizes the relationships between categorical variables. Methods: A CA was conducted using baseline data from the ongoing LIMIT (Lifestyle and Microbiom
papers.summary: This study applies correspondence analysis, a dimensionality-reduction technique for categorical data, to baseline data from the LIMIT trial to visualize relationships between maternal lifestyle factors (diet, physical activity, prepregnancy BMI) and gestational weight gain. The approach reveals hidden patterns in how these categorical variables cluster together, offering a visual exploratory framework for understanding complex maternal health associations.

papers.title: The Epigenetic Aging-Cancer Continuum: Biomarkers, Metabolism, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Aging and cancer form a biological continuum influenced by epigenomic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, cellular senescence, and loss of tissue homeostasis. Age-related epigenetic alterations can promote cancer, which exploits plasticity for evolution, immune evasion, metastasis, and resistance. Nutrition and metabolism affect this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl-donor availability, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, redox status, microbiome metabolites, and chromatin enzyme activity. Circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation, mutation-based ctDNA, fragmentom
papers.summary: This review argues that aging and cancer are not separate processes but a biological continuum driven by epigenetic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and cellular senescence. It highlights how nutrition and metabolism influence this continuum through one-carbon metabolism, methyl donors, acetyl-CoA/NAD+ balance, and microbiome metabolites, and discusses circulating biomarkers like cell-free DNA methylation and ctDNA for tracking it. The authors also consider therapeutic implications of targeting these epigenetic-metabolic links.

papers.title: Kernel Fatty Oils of Cinnamomum chago Alleviate Functional Constipation by Improving Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
papers.abstract: Cinnamomum chago (C. chago) B.S.Sun et H.L.Zhao, a rare tree species endemic to Yunnan Province of China, produces fruit kernels that are rich in fatty oils (CCKF); however, the potential health benefits of CCKF have not been previously reported.
papers.summary: This study investigates the health benefits of fatty oils extracted from the fruit kernels of Cinnamomum chago, a rare tree species endemic to Yunnan, China. The researchers found that these kernel fatty oils alleviate functional constipation by improving gut microbiota composition and enhancing intestinal barrier function. This is the first report of potential health benefits for this previously unstudied plant resource.

papers.title: Genetic Evidence for Metabolites Mediated Causal Inference Between Gut Microbiota and Venous Thromboembolism.
papers.abstract: Background: More efficient and safe preventive treatments for venous thromboembolism (VTE) are warranted to decrease the incidence of hemorrhage. Emerging evidence has highlighted the pivotal role of the intestinal microbiota alterations and their metabolites in the pathophysiology of VTE process. However, the specific species involved the VTE process and the potential underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The causal relationships between 82 species and VTE were assessed using two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) analyses. Instrumental variables (F > 10) without horizontal pleiotro
papers.summary: This study used two-sample Mendelian randomization to test whether gut microbiota species causally influence venous thromboembolism (VTE), and whether circulating metabolites mediate that effect. The authors identified specific bacterial taxa with genetically supported causal links to VTE and found evidence that certain metabolites act as intermediaries in this relationship.

papers.title: Microbial transmission and ecology of human and environmental microbial communities in childcare centers.
papers.abstract: Background Early-life microbial exposures profoundly impact lifelong health trajectories by shaping immune maturation and modulating disease risk, e.g. as described by the "hygiene hypothesis." Childcare facilities represent a critical yet understudied source of microbial exposures where preschool-aged children spend 7-10 hours daily during key developmental periods. This study presents the first multi-omic and multi-kingdom investigation of microbial transmission and community ecology across childcare environments, integrating microbiome samples from both high-touch and low-touch surfaces wit
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omic and multi-kingdom profiling to investigate how microbes are transmitted and structured across childcare environments, sampling both high-touch and low-touch surfaces alongside human-associated communities. It provides the first integrated view of microbial ecology and transmission dynamics in these understudied settings, which are critical for early-life immune exposure.

papers.title: Modulation of the Gut Microbiota by Prebiotics, Probiotics, and Psychobiotics and Its Impact on the Gut Microbiota-Brain Axis: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota-brain axis is a highly integrated bidirectional communication network operating through neural, neuroendocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways that maintain central nervous system homeostasis and has emerged as a promising complementary therapeutic target for neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how prebiotics, probiotics, and psychobiotics modulate the gut microbiota and influence the gut-brain axis. It synthesizes evidence on the neural, neuroendocrine, immune, and metabolic pathways through which these interventions may affect neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. The review positions microbiota-targeted approaches as promising complementary therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Gut, Oral, and Fungal Microbiota in Hypertension: A Multi-Compartment Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota is an established modulator of blood pressure, but the oral bacteriome and the fungal mycobiome have been examined largely in isolation from it and from each other. No previous synthesis has evaluated all three compartments within one analytical framework, or treated sex and ethnicity as primary analytical axes rather than adjustment covariates. Systematic review reported according to PRISMA 2020 and, for the synthesis, the SWiM guideline. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 30 June 2026. Observational human studies in adults re
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes human observational studies examining the gut bacteriome, oral bacteriome, and fungal mycobiome together in relation to hypertension, a multi-compartment approach not previously attempted. It also treats sex and ethnicity as primary analytical axes rather than covariates, aiming to clarify how microbial signatures across body sites associate with blood pressure.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review compares targeted (amplicon- and probe-based) and untargeted sequencing strategies for wastewater-based viral surveillance, highlighting trade-offs between sensitivity for known viruses and the ability to detect novel pathogens. It also discusses common bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater virome analysis, offering guidance for interpreting sequencing data in population-level monitoring.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterisation of Antibiotic Resistance in Anaerobic Digesters and Their Implications for Environmental Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in environmental systems represents an emerging One Health challenge, with anaerobic digesters potentially serving as reservoirs of resistance-associated genetic features. This study analysed four publicly available anaerobic digester shotgun metagenomic datasets (M2, M3, M12 and M17) retrieved from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive to characterise microbial functions, resistance-associated annotations and antibiotic target loci. The datasets were generated using Illumina HiSeq 2000 sequencing and analysed through quality assessment, assembly, functional annotation
papers.summary: This study re-analyzed four public shotgun metagenomic datasets from anaerobic digesters to profile microbial functions, antibiotic resistance annotations, and antibiotic target loci. It highlights anaerobic digesters as potential reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes, framing this as a One Health concern for environmental health.

papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterisation of a Metagenome-Derived CYP108D18 Reveals an Unusual Dioxygen-Bound State and Selective Hydrocarbon Hydroxylation.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes form a large superfamily of monooxygenases capable of oxidising diverse substrates. Among them, members of the CYP108 family are recognised for their role in monoterpenoid oxidation. In this study, we report the identification and characterisation of a new CYP108 family member, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome derived from microbial communities in a geothermal hot spring located in northern Queensland, Australia. Taxonomic binning associated CYP108D18 with a Novosphingobium species, a genus well-known for its bioremediation potential. CYP108D18 was heterolo
papers.summary: Researchers identified a new cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome of microbes living in an Australian geothermal hot spring. The enzyme, traced to a Novosphingobium species, was structurally and functionally characterized, revealing an unusual dioxygen-bound state and the ability to selectively hydroxylate hydrocarbons. This highlights geothermal metagenomes as a source of novel biocatalysts with potential bioremediation or biotechnological applications.

papers.title: From Rhizosphere to Resistance: Microbe-Plant Interactions in Eco-Smart Biocontrol.
papers.abstract: The increasing limitations of chemical pesticides such as environmental pollution, pathogen resistance, and threats to human and ecosystem health have increased the demand for sustainable, biologically based crop protection methods. Eco-smart biocontrol has emerged as a game-changing paradigm that uses beneficial microorganisms associated with plants to suppress phytopathogens, boost plant immunity, and make agroecosystems more resilient over time. Moving beyond traditional single-strain biocontrol, eco-smart biocontrol integrates multi-omics discovery, artificial intelligence-assisted predict
papers.summary: This review examines how beneficial microorganisms in the plant rhizosphere can be harnessed for sustainable, biologically based crop protection as an alternative to chemical pesticides. It highlights the emerging 'eco-smart biocontrol' paradigm, which moves beyond single-strain approaches by integrating multi-omics discovery and AI-assisted prediction to suppress pathogens and boost plant immunity.

papers.title: Comparing the Performance of Double-Stranded and Single-Stranded DNA Libraries for Ancient Oral Microbiome Reconstruction.
papers.abstract: DNA library construction methods can affect the recovery of ancient DNA, thus influencing downstream analyses. While single-stranded library preparation (ssLib) has been shown to outperform double-stranded (dsLib) for highly degraded vertebrate host DNA, especially for samples older than 40,000 years, few studies have examined how library protocols shape ancient microbial community reconstruction. Here, we compare the sequencing output of paired ssLib and dsLib dental calculus libraries generated from 12 Neanderthals and two Chalcolithic humans, prepared using implementations of the Gansauge e
papers.summary: This study compares single-stranded (ssLib) and double-stranded (dsLib) DNA library preparation methods for reconstructing ancient oral microbiomes from dental calculus of 12 Neanderthals and two Chalcolithic humans. While ssLib is known to outperform dsLib for highly degraded host DNA, the authors assess whether this advantage extends to microbial community reconstruction. The work provides methodological guidance for choosing library protocols in ancient microbiome studies.

papers.title: The Plant-Microbe Alliance for Environmental Restoration: From Nature-Inspired Solutions to Engineered Ecological Recovery.
papers.abstract: According to the United Nations, up to 40% of the world's terrestrial ecosystems are degraded and in need of ecological restoration. Here, we argue that ecosystem restoration requires not only the reintroduction of plant species but also the recovery of the biological interactions that sustain ecosystem functioning. Plants and their associated microbiomes form integrated functional units in which microorganisms contribute to nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, contaminant degradation and ecosystem resilience. These plant-microbe partnerships therefore represent a new opportunity for environmen
papers.summary: This review argues that restoring degraded ecosystems requires not just replanting vegetation but also re-establishing the beneficial microbial communities that partner with plants. It highlights how plant-microbiome alliances drive nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, and contaminant degradation, and proposes engineering these interactions for ecological recovery.

papers.title: Converting Equol Nonproducers to Producers: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
papers.abstract: Soy isoflavones have been associated with benefits for menopausal symptoms, cardiovascular health, and cognitive function, yet randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in Western countries have produced inconsistent results. A key factor may be equol, a metabolite of daidzein with stronger estrogenic and antioxidant effects, produced at lower rates in Western than in East Asian populations. This systematic review evaluates RCTs aimed at converting equol nonproducers to producers (CRD420251038428). We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for RCTs published between 1991 and 2025. Twelve RCTs (n
papers.summary: This systematic review examines 12 randomized clinical trials testing whether equol nonproducers—individuals who cannot convert the soy isoflavone daidzein into the more bioactive metabolite equol—can be converted into producers through dietary or probiotic interventions. The review addresses why soy isoflavone trials show inconsistent health benefits, particularly between Western and East Asian populations with differing equol production rates.

papers.title: Personalized whole-body modeling links gut microbiota to metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome has been linked to metabolic disturbances in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the mechanisms by which gut microbes might influence metabolic dysfunction in AD remain poorly understood. Previously, gut microbiome-personalized whole-body models of human metabolism have been applied to predict how altered gut microbiome compositions may influence metabolites in the blood of healthy aging individuals with increased risk of AD. However, these previous results have not been validated in AD. In this study, we aimed to test these prior predictions in a cohort of AD dementia
papers.summary: This study uses personalized whole-body metabolic models informed by gut microbiome composition to test whether microbial changes can explain metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease dementia patients. It validates prior predictions from healthy aging cohorts in an AD cohort, linking specific gut microbes to blood metabolite alterations. The work supports a mechanistic role for the gut microbiome in AD-associated metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: From predicted bacteriocins to ecological function.
papers.abstract: Genome and metagenome mining have uncovered large repertoires of predicted bacteriocin loci, but ecological interpretation has lagged behind discovery. This review uses bacteriocins as a focused model for a broader problem in antimicrobial gene prediction: sequence identifies encoded potential, but it does not establish expression, product deployment, target engagement, or community-level consequence. We distinguish four forms of bacteriocin "silence": transcriptional silence, where loci are not detectably expressed under tested conditions; conditional silence, where expression or activity eme
papers.summary: This review argues that while genome and metagenome mining has revealed many predicted bacteriocin loci, sequence data alone cannot establish whether these antimicrobial peptides are actually expressed, deployed, or functionally active in microbial communities. It distinguishes four forms of bacteriocin 'silence'—transcriptional, conditional, and others—to frame a broader challenge in antimicrobial gene prediction: moving from encoded potential to demonstrated ecological function.

papers.title: Cross-platform, multi-cohort identification of a caries microbial signature.
papers.abstract: To identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with caries using a cross-platform, multi-cohort design.
papers.summary: This study uses a cross-platform, multi-cohort design to identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with dental caries. By integrating data across different sequencing platforms and patient cohorts, the authors aim to find microbial markers that consistently distinguish caries-affected individuals. The resulting signature could improve caries risk assessment and guide microbiome-based prevention strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiota characteristics of gastric cancer patients across distinct pathological stages and their associations with tumor and paratumor mucosal microbiota.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is closely associated with microbial dysbiosis; however, the spatial-temporal characteristics of the gut, paracancerous, and intratumoral microbiomes, as well as their interrelationships during tumor progression, remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize these microbiomes in 85 GC patients from Northwest China using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and functional annotation. Clinical samples included feces, tumor tissues, and paratumor mucosal tissues (≥5 cm from the tumor margin), enabling comprehensive profiling of microbial composition at the phylum,
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to profile the fecal, tumor, and paratumor mucosal microbiomes of 85 gastric cancer patients from Northwest China across different pathological stages. It characterizes how microbial composition and functional potential differ spatially (gut vs. tumor vs. adjacent tissue) and temporally (across cancer stages), revealing associations between these microbial communities and tumor progression.

papers.title: Functional organization outweighs spatial separation in structuring microbial communities across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume.
papers.abstract: Petroleum-hydrocarbon plumes in groundwater are shaped by hydrological transport, redox conditions, and indigenous microbial activity. However, it remains unclear whether spatial differences among groundwater microbiomes primarily reflect physical separation among wells or ecological reorganization associated with distinct attenuation states within a plume.
papers.summary: This study examines whether microbial community differences across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume are driven mainly by physical distance between sampling wells or by ecological reorganization tied to different contaminant attenuation states. The authors find that functional organization of the communities outweighs spatial separation, indicating that plume chemistry and degradation processes, rather than geography alone, structure the microbiomes.

papers.title: Microbial niches at the One Health interface: linking environmental factors, biomes, and disease dynamics.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities shape life at every stratum of environmental hierarchy, ranging from a wide spectrum of functionalities such as nutrient cycling processes that support ecosystem functioning in soil biome to those of intricate balance between disease causal and responsive immune defenses in animals. This review explores the roles of microbial niches in shaping pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination, and host-microbe interactions at the human-animal-environment interface. Emphasis is placed on microbial community assembly, environmental drivers of pathogen survi
papers.summary: This review examines how microbial communities at the human-animal-environment interface influence pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance spread, and host-microbe interactions. It emphasizes community assembly rules and environmental drivers that determine pathogen survival across interconnected biomes. The work frames these dynamics within the One Health framework linking environmental factors to disease emergence.

papers.title: Combined abdominal and transcranial photobiomodulation is associated with fecal microbiome restructuring: a systems microbiology pre-post case report.
papers.abstract: Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been proposed as a non-invasive strategy capable of modulating mitochondrial, inflammatory, vascular, and gut-brain axis-related pathways. However, its potential effects on fecal microbiome ecology in neurobehavioral conditions remain poorly characterized. This case report describes paired fecal microbiome findings before and after a 90-day combined abdominal and transcranial PBM protocol in a 6-year-old female with autism spectrum disorder and chronic constipation. PBM was delivered daily using a 1064-nm near-infrared LED device with 54 mW/cm2 irradiance, applied
papers.summary: This case report describes fecal microbiome changes in a 6-year-old girl with autism spectrum disorder and chronic constipation before and after a 90-day combined abdominal and transcranial photobiomodulation (near-infrared LED) protocol. The study reports restructuring of the fecal microbiome following treatment, suggesting PBM may influence gut microbiome ecology via gut-brain axis-related pathways. As a single pre-post case report, the findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive.

papers.title: Bronchoalveolar Lavage Microbiota in Critically Ill Patients with Aspiration Pneumonia: An Exploratory Comparison with Community-Acquired Pneumonia and Analysis of Gemella Detection and Mortality.
papers.abstract: Aspiration pneumonia (AP) is a common and severe infection among critically ill older adults, but its lower respiratory tract microbiota and clinical associations remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory study characterizes the bronchoalveolar lavage microbiota of critically ill patients with aspiration pneumonia and compares it to community-acquired pneumonia, with a specific focus on Gemella detection and its relationship to mortality. The findings suggest distinct microbial signatures in aspiration pneumonia that may have prognostic implications.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics-guided drug development in inflammatory bowel disease: from mucosal immune niches to precision therapy.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are now treated with an expanding set of biologics and small molecules, yet treatment selection remains largely empirical. Primary non-response, secondary loss of response, incomplete mucosal healing, fibrostenosis, and fistulizing disease show that conventional clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers do not capture how disease is organized within tissue. This review argues that the inflamed intestine is better viewed as a set of spatially structured mucosal immune niches rather than as uniform inflammation, with epithelial, myeloid, lymphoid, st
papers.summary: This review argues that inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) should be understood as a collection of spatially organized mucosal immune niches rather than uniform inflammation, and that conventional clinical and bulk molecular markers fail to capture this tissue-level organization. It proposes that spatial multi-omics approaches can guide more precise drug development and therapy selection for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics, Machine Learning, and Single-Cell Analysis Provide Insights into Potential Multi-Target Candidate Mechanisms of Combined MAGL11 and Icaritin in Alleviating Imidazole Propionate-Driven Metabolic Intestinal Injury.
papers.abstract: Unhealthy diets, especially high red meat intake, induce gut dysbiosis and abnormal accumulation of a harmful histidine metabolite imidazole propionate (IMP), thereby promoting ulcerative colitis (UC) development. Although combined treatment with a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) and icaritin (Y003) exerts combined therapeutic effects in the classical DSS‑induced UC model, its protective effects and molecular mechanisms against IMP‑driven metabolic model remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether combining a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) with icaritin (Y003) can protect against intestinal injury caused by imidazole propionate (IMP), a harmful metabolite produced by gut bacteria after high red meat consumption. Using integrated multi-omics, machine learning, and single-cell analysis, the authors identify potential multi-target mechanisms underlying the combined treatment's protective effects in a metabolic model of ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Correlation analysis between tongue hyperspectral imaging and tongue coating microbiota and feasibility study for early screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus status.
papers.abstract: To investigate the feasibility of applying hyperspectral imaging technology combined with machine learning algorithms for early non-invasive screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
papers.summary: This study explores whether hyperspectral imaging of the tongue, combined with machine learning, can non-invasively detect type 2 diabetes and whether imaging features correlate with tongue coating microbiota. The authors report that this combined approach shows promise as an early screening tool for T2DM status. The work is preliminary and based on a small, single-cohort design.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism: a critical bridge linking gut microbiota to depression.
papers.abstract: Depression is a major global public health challenge with limitations in current therapies. Emerging evidence highlights that gut microbiota (GM) critically regulates the gut-brain axis via tryptophan (Trp) metabolism. Trp is metabolized through host-directed serotonin (5-HT) and kynurenine (KYN) pathways, as well as microbiota-specific indole derivative pathways. In depression, gut dysbiosis shifts Trp metabolism toward the KYN pathway, leading to accumulation of neurotoxic metabolites such as quinolinic acid and reduced 5-HT synthesis. Microbiota-derived indoles, functioning as key aryl hydr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that gut microbiota regulate the gut-brain axis through tryptophan metabolism, with depression associated with a dysbiotic shift toward the neurotoxic kynurenine pathway and reduced serotonin synthesis. Microbiota-derived indole derivatives are highlighted as key modulators of this process, suggesting tryptophan metabolism as a therapeutic target for depression.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures in mild cognitive impairment: a scoping review of microbial taxa and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: To identify systematically the typical gut microbiota in mild cognitive impairment patients and its association in disease progression. Systematically identify microbial taxa consistently associated with Mild Cognitive Impairment.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically compiles studies on gut microbiota composition in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), identifying microbial taxa that are consistently altered compared to healthy controls. It highlights potential links between specific gut bacteria and MCI progression, suggesting clinical implications for early detection or intervention.

papers.title: NeighborFinder: an R package inferring local microbial network around a species of interest.
papers.abstract: Understanding interactions from microbiome data is a central aspect in microbial ecology, as it provides insights into ecosystem stability, disease mechanisms, and can be used to design synthetic communities. Current network inference tools reconstruct global networks from co-abundance data, which means they capture the overall correlation structure for the entire set of taxa considered. These approaches are computationally intensive and suboptimal when the focus is on the local neighborhood of one or a few taxa of interest.
papers.summary: NeighborFinder is an R package that infers the local microbial interaction network surrounding a species of interest, rather than reconstructing the entire global co-abundance network. This targeted approach is computationally lighter and better suited for studies focused on one or a few taxa, with applications in microbial ecology, disease research, and synthetic community design.

papers.title: Crotoxin from Crotalus durissus terrificus impairs the establishment of chemically induced colitis in mice associated with formyl peptide receptor signaling.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs) arise from a breakdown in tolerance to intestinal microbiota and are characterized by exacerbated inflammatory responses. Epithelial cells of the gastrointestinal tract play a central role in maintaining barrier integrity and orchestrating immune responses; however, the mechanisms underlying epithelial dysfunction and uncontrolled inflammation remain incompletely understood. Crotoxin (CTX), the main component of Crotalus d. terrificus venom, exhibits immunomodulatory activity, making it a promising tool to investigate epithelial-immune interactions in intesti
papers.summary: This study shows that crotoxin, a component of rattlesnake venom, can prevent the development of chemically induced colitis in mice. The protective effect appears to work through formyl peptide receptor signaling, highlighting a potential immunomodulatory mechanism relevant to inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning uncovers core seminal microbial signatures in idiopathic oligoasthenospermia.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have confirmed that changes in semen microbiota are closely related to male oligoasthenospermia(OA). However, current research only qualitatively describes the differences in the microbial community, fails to screen out core markers with independent discriminatory value, and also fails to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of the microbial community, resulting in insufficient research on the diagnostic value of the semen microbiota in oligoasthenospermia.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study applies interpretable machine learning to semen microbiota data to identify core microbial signatures that can distinguish idiopathic oligoasthenospermia (OA) from controls. Unlike prior qualitative descriptions, it screens for markers with independent discriminatory value and quantitatively evaluates the diagnostic efficacy of the semen microbial community. The work suggests specific seminal microbes may serve as diagnostic biomarkers for male infertility.

papers.title: Beyond a universal obesity microbiome signature: pre-intervention heterogeneity and a framework for baseline profiling.
papers.abstract: Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize obesity-associated microbial alterations, this review reframes the recurrent inconsistency of human obesity microbiome findings as an informative consequence of pre-intervention heterogeneity rather than merely failed replication or analytical noise. We integrate biological and contextual determinants of baseline microbiota variation with methodological and analytical sources of heterogeneity into a unified framework for interpreting why microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and functional signals differ across individuals, populations, an
papers.summary: This review argues that inconsistent findings in human obesity microbiome studies are not simply noise or failed replication, but reflect meaningful pre-intervention heterogeneity in baseline microbiota across individuals and populations. It proposes a unified framework integrating biological, contextual, methodological, and analytical factors to guide baseline profiling and interpretation of obesity-related microbial signals.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Etiology-Specific Evidence, Mechanisms, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) usually develops in patients with chronic liver disease and remains a major cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Increasing evidence suggests that dysbiosis of the gut microbiota is related to hepatocarcinogenesis through the gut-liver axis. Patients with HCC often show enrichment of pro-inflammatory or endotoxin-producing bacteria and loss of short-chain fatty acid-producing and barrier-protective taxa. These changes may increase intestinal permeability and microbial translocation and may contribute to chronic hepatic inflammation, immune disturbance, and me
papers.summary: This review examines how disruptions in gut microbial communities contribute to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through the gut-liver axis, highlighting that HCC patients often show increased pro-inflammatory and endotoxin-producing bacteria alongside reduced beneficial short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa. These microbial shifts may promote liver cancer by increasing intestinal permeability, microbial translocation, and chronic hepatic inflammation, though the authors note translational challenges remain.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration of the vaginal microbiome and inflammatory proteome for non-invasive prediction of infertility: a machine learning approach.
papers.abstract: Infertility remains a global health challenge that often necessitates invasive and costly diagnostic procedures. While the vaginal microenvironment is known to influence reproductive health, its potential as a source of non-invasive biomarkers for infertility remains insufficiently explored. This study integrated vaginal microbiome and inflammatory proteomic profiling using machine learning to develop and validate an objective, non-invasive diagnostic model for identifying women at high risk of infertility.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study combined vaginal microbiome profiling with inflammatory protein measurements and applied machine learning to build a non-invasive model for predicting infertility risk in women. The integrated multi-omics approach outperformed single-data-type models, suggesting vaginal microbial and inflammatory signatures could offer a cheaper, less invasive alternative to current diagnostic procedures.
